messages:
Maya Patel: FYI customer (ACME) hit a sudden p99 latency spike on /v1/generate ~2026-03-14T09:12Z, p95 stayed ~300ms but p99 jumped to 5-8s, no 5xxs. They call it "request pile-up" — says most requests sit in admission for seconds before scheduling. Customer provided req id 01F8X9-ACME-9432. Can we triage? :eyes:

Jorge Ramos: Ack. Which region & model? Hosted or Dedicated? Any recent deploys around 09:00Z? Can you paste a small repro curl and a few tail logs (admission/worker logs) with the req id?

Maya Patel: Region: us-west-2, hosted, model: rdx-7b-q4 (default). No customer-side code change. Repro curl below (works for us to reproduce the slow tail):
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-REDACT" \
  -H "X-Request-ID: 01F8X9-ACME-9432" \
  -d '{"model":"rdx-7b-q4","prompt":"short"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Logs (excerpt):
```
[2026-03-14T09:11:58Z] admission: enqueued req=01F8X9-ACME-9432 wait_ms=3120 pool=inference-prod
[2026-03-14T09:11:58Z] worker-132: start processing req=01F8X9-ACME-9432 seq_len=512
[2026-03-14T09:12:01Z] worker-132: finished req=01F8X9-ACME-9432 elapsed_ms=2860
[2026-03-14T09:12:02Z] admission: enqueue_size=84 drain_rate=5/s backpressure=true
```
Customer says similar numbers across many requests; not isolated.

infra-oncall-bot: ALERT: p99 latency > 2s for /v1/generate in us-west-2 (last 5m). Triggered at 2026-03-14T09:12:05Z. Recent deploys: runtime/admission-config:v2026-03-14-1.

Liu Chen: Looking at metrics — admission queue depth for inference-prod jumped from median 8 -> 72 at ~09:10Z. CPU on workers is fine, but inflight token memory looks high (long seqs causing worker occupancy). The new admission parameters we rolled earlier this morning lowered per-worker max inflight to reduce OOM risk; sounds like we overconstrained concurrency for this workload. Suspect "inflight_per_worker" cap is too low for rdx-7b-q4 when seq_len distribution skews small+long tail.

Kavita Singh: Proposed immediate mitigations (low-risk):
- Temporarily increase per-worker inflight cap for inference-prod to previous value.
- Enable burst pool (reserve extra workers) for hosted tier to absorb the queue.
- Route traffic for long prompt customers to fallback smaller model bundle if backlog persists.

Jorge Ramos: Can we do a one-click hotfix: rollback admission-config to yesterday's revision and spin up +30 workers in burst pool? That should unclog admission. If rollback takes too long, we can bump inflight cap via runtime flags.

Liu Chen: Agreed. Quick config diff I see: the rollout changed from:
```yaml
admission:
  inflight_per_worker: 12
  queue_timeout_ms: 45000
```
to:
```yaml
admission:
  inflight_per_worker: 6   # new conservative default
  queue_timeout_ms: 45000
```
Halving inflight_per_worker doubled queueing pressure under the same request load.

Kavita Singh: I'll trigger the burst pool scale and a rollback if infra-op approves. Command I'll run: 
```bash
# scale burst pool (internal tool)
rb scale-pool --env prod --pool inference-prod-burst --delta 30
# rollback admission config
rb deploy-config --name runtime/admission-config --rev v2026-03-13-4
```

infra-oncall-bot: runbook action requested by @Kavita Singh. Approve? :thumbsup: / :thumbsdown:

Jorge Ramos: :thumbsup: approve. Also set a temporary route rule: send 10% of traffic to rdx-3b-fast to reduce load.

infra-oncall-bot: Action logs: scale-pool started (job id 5443). deploy-config rollback started (job id 5444).

infra-oncall-bot: SUCCESS job 5443 - burst pool scaled +30 workers (completed 2026-03-14T09:18:40Z).

deploy-bot: SUCCESS job 5444 - runtime/admission-config rolled back to v2026-03-13-4 (completed 2026-03-14T09:19:12Z).

Jorge Ramos: After hotfix metrics: admission queue depth dropped from ~72 -> 9 within 2 mins. p95 ~320ms, p99 ~720ms (us-west-2). Customer confirmed improved experience.

Maya Patel: Customer (ACME) reports latency back to normal & said they will do further validation. They asked for root cause summary and steps we took.

Kavita Singh: Summary for CS: root cause = aggressive admission config change this morning that halved inflight_per_worker; effect = high queueing when seq-length distribution allowed many small/short requests which kept workers occupied but limited inflight concurrency, causing pile-up and p99 regressions. Fixes: rolled back admission-config to previous rev, scaled burst pool +30, applied temporary 10% routing to rdx-3b-fast for tail reduction. Follow-ups: re-evaluate safe default for inflight_per_worker with workload signals, add canary metrics for queue depth during config rollouts, and add automated rollback when queue depth spike > 3x baseline.

support-bot: Logged incident notes and notified CS (ticket #INC-2026-ACME-942). Customer follow-up assigned to Maya. Closing thread unless more evidence emerges. :white_check_mark:
